title: Manual versus GenAI generation of preparatory testing artifacts
summary: Postgraduate software-testing students first create use cases, traceability matrices, test cases, and scripts manually as a group. They then reproduce the artifacts individually with ChatGPT or Copilot and answer eleven questions comparing coverage, accuracy, efficiency, limitations, and the continuing need for human testing.

sources.title: Exploring the Integration of Generative AI Tools in Software Testing Education: A Case Study on ChatGPT and Copilot for Preparatory Testing Artifacts in Postgraduate Learning

locator.section: III. Methodology, B. Assignment Design and Study Framework

sources.evidence_quote: Students initially created preparatory testing artifacts manually as a group deliverable. Following this, they were assigned an individual assignment to generate the same artifacts using LLM tools.

assessment.summary: Generate equivalent software-testing artifacts manually and with GenAI, then critically compare the two production methods.
student_actions: Create testing artifacts manually with a group.
Individually prompt an LLM to generate equivalent artifacts.
Iteratively refine prompts using application-specific information.

inputs.description: Custom travel application in Term 1 or MoneyManagerEx documentation and application in Term 2

student_role.description: Students use an assigned LLM to reproduce testing artifacts and compare them with artifacts previously created manually.

grading.method: Assignment artifacts and analytical responses were assessed with question-specific rubrics; exact course weight and rubric values are not reported in extractable text.

criteria.criterion: Critical analysis of AI strengths and limitations

reported_results: The analysis included 26 of 61 Term 1 submissions and 21 of 35 Term 2 submissions that scored at least 90%.
Students concluded that LLMs can augment but not replace manual testing.
